metadata_scope_notes.work_id: title:ruck 2021 the laws and the land
metadata_scope_notes.note: The book studies Kahnawà:ke’s relationship with Canada and the imposition of colonial law. Its opening separates this focus from a Kanien’kehá:ka history and from a military invasion, while acknowledging a background threat of military violence. The current Maritimes/Upper Canada Loyalist and broad post-1815 migration citations need event-specific passages or other support; this focused study alone does not establish those broader narratives.

The article is a prosopography of named cultural practitioners in Bithynia. This indexed opening does not establish population totals or replacement. The saved Astakos note cites p.74 for a broad Nicomedes/Astakos summary, already qualified against an exact destruction-transfer date; p.74 was not newly obtained.

Title 64787 identifies Zapelloni Pavia’s study of Umbrian cult places. The book’s regional religious scope is more specific than a generic Gracchan-land label. Indexed chapter and book metadata do not newly verify CIL I²719, the 132 BCE boundary date or later restoration; the current case’s limits and the distinction between ancient allotment and restoration remain. Ritual continuity is not evidence that dispossession did not occur.
